tasks.task: Turn a goal into a project plan

items.when: When a project is agreed: a client job signed, a launch, a redesign, a system change or a move
When the goal needs a finish line, tasks, owners, effort ranges, dependencies and milestones
When the goal is vague, to ask the few questions that matter before any planning
When a spec exists, to split it into small ordered tasks, each with a way to check it is done
When the project spans several teams and needs a charter, owners and dependencies
When the project could be phased or done in one push, to compare two plans with money and dates

tasks.task: Build the risk and assumption log

items.when: When the plan exists and each risk needs a trigger, an owner and a response
When several parts must meet on one date, to find the joins where things fail
When several projects run at once, to score risks across them and balance people
When the log lists only small risks, to look for the one shock that would end the project

tasks.task: Write a client or team kickoff brief

items.when: When a project is about to start and everyone needs the same picture of scope, roles and timeline
When it is a client project, to get the brief and an agenda only if a meeting is worth holding
When the brief is for a creative job, to try a version built on goal, audience, tone and limits
When channels and update dates are unclear, to set them and where decisions are recorded
Before the brief is sent, to read it as the client and list what they would have to ask

tasks.task: Write the weekly status update

items.when: Each week on a running project, to say where things stand on one page
When the reader wants status, risks and decisions needed in a fixed monthly or weekly format
When leaders, the team and the client each need the update at a different depth
When the news is bad, to pitch the note to the person who must act on it
Before the update goes out, to check every date, cost and percent against the plan and notes

tasks.task: Run weekly project control

items.when: At every review point, on the same day, for each running project
When budget, schedule and spend are known, to get cost and schedule indexes and a finish cost
Each week, to see where work waits and whether the current fix should stay
After each review meeting, to check last week's actions and set the next agenda
When the status is green by habit, to check the data behind each measure and the delivery gaps

tasks.task: Write a client project scope

items.when: When deliverables, revisions, exclusions, assumptions and the change process must be written down
When the project is a website, to get goals, users, features and a page plan in one brief
When each requirement needs an owner, a build, a test and an approval beside it
Before the scope is signed, to read it as the client and find what could be argued later

tasks.task: Turn a new ask into a change request

items.when: When a client asks for more and it needs a polite note with time, cost and a choice
Before replying, to compare the ask with the signed scope and the team's hours
When the change is to a system or process and needs impact, risks and rollback steps
When the draft sounds annoyed, to get a version the client wants to say yes to
Before sending, to check new work is kept as proposed and priced, not folded in

tasks.task: Estimate cost and time with ranges

items.when: When a software, website or other project needs low, likely and high figures with assumptions
Before estimating, to split the spec into small tasks that can each be sized
When the team builds with AI agents, to get time ranges that allow for it
When the estimate is done, to correct it by how similar projects really went
When the estimate must become a first client quote with terms
When a date is promised from hope, to turn it into a dated forecast with a base rate

tasks.task: Check a developer or agency quote

items.when: When a non-developer has a quote and wants to know what is vague, missing or out of line
When there is a spec, to list the tasks a full quote should cover and the gaps to settle
When the quoted timeline looks short, to test it against projects like it
When the quote comes with terms, to flag the risky ones in plain words

tasks.task: Offer scope options that fit the budget

items.when: When the estimate is over budget and the client needs options with what each drops
When the date is fixed, to keep it with half the scope: the core first, the rest parked
When the plan keeps growing, to shape a smaller bet and list what to say no to
When the team cannot agree what to cut, to pick a ranking method that fits
When there are two ways to spend the budget, to show both with money and dates
When every feature is called essential, to cut to a first version that is still useful

tasks.task: Re-forecast a project in progress

items.when: When work done so far shows the first estimate was off and a new range is needed
When spend and progress to date are known, to project the finish cost and date
When the slip repeats, to map where work waits before promising a new date
When the new forecast is bad news, to tell the client or owner plainly

tasks.task: Plan team capacity for the next six weeks

items.when: When the team must decide whether it can take a project or promise a date
When people and projects are listed, to see who is overloaded and what can be taken on
Before a date is promised, to see the options and their risks with a draft reply

tasks.task: Run a project wrap-up and lessons review

items.when: When a project has finished or stopped and the team wants to learn without blame
When people hold back in reviews, to run one where they tell the truth
When feedback is collected, to sort what went well, what did not and actions with owners
When the review is done, to write one page of what to repeat and what to change
When closing a client job, to record what was delivered, accepted and still open

tasks.task: Build a content inventory and new page list

items.when: When a redesign starts and each current page needs a keep, update, merge or cut call
When there is a list of the site's pages, to mark each with a call and a reason
When the new page list needs a hierarchy, navigation and URL plan

tasks.task: Write the redesign brief for a designer or agency

items.when: When the why, the audience and the page list are agreed and a designer needs one brief
When goals, users, features and design tokens should sit in one scoped document
When the client cannot describe the look, to pin down tone and feel in four answers
When the client must pick a direction, to show three first screens before the brief is fixed
Before the brief goes out, to read it as the designer and list what they would have to ask

tasks.task: Plan a site move with a redirect map

items.when: When a site moves platform or theme and search traffic must survive the move
When old and new sites are named, to plan a move that keeps rank, links and bookmarks
When domains or subdomains change, to lay out DNS and redirect rules
Before launch, to save the site's search state and be warned if rankings or tags slip after
After launch, to audit crawling, indexing and structure on the new site

tasks.task: Plan a launch or go-live

items.when: When the build is near done and the last steps to launch need owners and dates
When a release is set, to get a pre-launch checklist, a staged rollout and a rollback plan
When a physical product launches, to date every step from samples to warehouse
When an internal tool is rolled out, to list open blockers and record the go decision
In the last week, to check the joins between teams and what gives way under load

tasks.task: Turn meeting notes into minutes and owned actions

items.when: When rough notes need short minutes with decisions, owners, dates and open questions
When actions are spread over a meeting and several threads, to make one list with follow-ups
When you sit in the meeting and want fuller notes without a bot in the call

tasks.task: Map stakeholders and plan project communication

items.when: When many people are affected, to place each on a power and interest grid
When updates are ad hoc, to set channels, dates and a record of approvals
When the project changes how staff work, to plan messages and adoption

tasks.task: Write requirements and acceptance checks

items.when: When the request is vague, to ask the few questions that settle it, with default answers
When one feature needs goals, non-goals, success measures and acceptance checks
When the developers work from stories, to write them with acceptance criteria
Before sign-off, to see that every requirement has a build, a test and an approval

tasks.task: Find why a project keeps slipping

items.when: When deadlines slip again and again, to map the delay and back causes with records
When one failure keeps returning, to build a chain of whys checked against facts
When the cause may be overbooking, to compare the hours promised with the hours there are

tasks.task: Plan a system or supplier change

items.when: When the change needs a plan with a cut-over date, owners and a way back
When a tool or supplier is being replaced, to plan notice dates and a staged switch
When data moves between tools, to map fields, checks and a rollback path

always.when: Before a plan, scope or update is shared, to catch typos and a deliverable named two ways

helpers.when: When an estimate or quote check needs someone to judge the technical work itself
When the redesign moves from brief to actual page designs and a build
When the site move puts a lot of search traffic at risk and needs a full audit
When the new site must meet accessibility rules for the client's region
When the project is an event and needs a run sheet, venue and supplier plan
When the question is what to build and why, not when and by whom

gaps: No library item builds a general project plan with dependencies, a critical path and milestones for a non-software project
No library item builds a risk and assumption log with triggers and owners, or runs a premortem
No library item checks a developer or agency quote for vague lines, missing work and prices out of line
No library item re-forecasts a project in progress from work done against the first estimate
No library item writes a client scope statement with revisions, exclusions and a change process
No library item builds a redirect map from old to new URLs or checks it after launch
No library item pulls a content inventory from a live site with traffic and a keep or cut call per page
No library item plans an office move, or draws a timeline or Gantt view of a plan
No library item writes a team capacity plan across several client projects week by week
No library item offers clearly different formats of a status update to test with a client
